evidence_loop.label: Codex installs that ran main under a released version: install-cache discovery and pin diagnostics (ADR-0061 S1-S3)
evidence_loop.summary: Codex's catalog entries are local and its marketplace is a git clone of main, so a Codex start whose upgrade succeeds after main moves re-clones it and force-reinstalls every plugin under an unchanged version, and cross-plugin discovery on Codex also read that clone. S1 and S2 make companion discovery and the sibling resolvers prefer the caller's own install cache and drop the clone as a candidate, keeping explicit overrides and documented fallbacks; S3 makes doctor report each Codex install against its catalog pin with target, installed version and content identity kept apart. One release commit cut nine tags, the floor ADR-0061 Decision 5 (a) is to name. Installed from it, the proof's permission and peer-smoke runs executed the installed companions from each host's cache where the preceding proof, run from the same checkout, executed the checkout's. Parity reads the same blocked 87% on the same compat criterion. Catalog pinning (S4) and machine acceptance (S6) remain.

install_method: Claude: marketplace update, then settings executor settings-20260925T054211Z-52f408 (8 claude plugin update, 0 failed); installs at gitCommitSha 807f76a. Codex: three marketplace upgrades timed out at the 30 s clone limit amid slow GitHub downloads; one then ran with a GIT_CONFIG insteadOf, in that command's environment only, to a bare local mirror of main at 807f76a, reinstalling all eight.
narrative:
**The effect only a release could show is in the proof's own execution.** Both this proof and the 0.97.4 proof ran from this repository. That one's permission proof and deep peer smoke executed the checkout's companions/codex-companion.mjs and companions/claude-companion.mjs, with the Codex marketplace clone among the Codex-direction candidates; this one executed the installed companions 0.4.2 from Claude's cache and from Codex's cache, the Codex direction with no other candidate. The workflow-continuation proof ran the Claude-installed engineer both times. It does not show Decision 5 (b): no fresh Codex session was asked to resolve each sibling, and the receivers were not re-rendered.

**The parity reading is not this loop's effect.** Its one blocked criterion sits on compat-20260918T040728Z-6f1daa, the same run that blocked the 0.97.4 proof. The new codex_install_identity reads unpinned and unknown for all eight, which is the correct pre-activation answer. receivers reads stale as an intended effect: S3 registered the v1 statusline and notify shims, current in the 0.97.4 proof, as legacy shapes, and re-rendering them is S6.

**Delivery is byte-identical for all eight packages, on Codex by circumstance.** Every tracked file at each release tag blob-compares equal, owner-exec bit included and no extra file, in Claude's cache and in Codex's cache, 446 files per host; runtime reads 3216ed0992e59c9c6bbd8d65ed8485ec0c55f4411c279dae91af3fd4c5e0af04 over 122 files under the scorecard's path-first recipe, control-verified by reproducing 0.97.4's published digest. Codex matches because main held the release's package bytes when it refreshed; until S4 pins the catalog, a later package-path commit on main reaches Codex under these versions at the next successful refresh. The packaged baseline hash moved because C51 changed one sentence, not because the baseline was re-observed.

**Codex's refresh needed a workaround, disclosed rather than hidden.** Three codex plugin marketplace upgrade attempts timed out at Codex's 30 s clone limit. Measured separately, GitHub downloads to this machine were slow (codeload 65-100 KB/s, a direct git clone stalled) while another registry served 1.5 MB/s. A short codex exec started the background re-clone and left a staging directory with no HEAD when it exited. One upgrade then ran with GIT_CONFIG_* set only in that command's environment, redirecting the clone to a bare local mirror of main at 807f76a, the commit GitHub served; the snapshot's recorded source and origin stay on GitHub.

**Hooks were re-attested on version binding alone.** No Codex hook file changed between the attested and released tags of the four hook-bearing packages and the Codex CLI stayed at 0.156.1, but the attestation binds installed versions (Decision 8), so after the Codex refresh the owner re-reviewed /hooks and settings-20260925T061733Z-5344b0 was recorded.
